thread:
maria.g: quick heads-up — flash-attention upstream merged a change that alters softmax epilog ordering, we saw it flip perf on our quantized path in nightly runs. reproducer and numbers below.

sam.k: ugh, saw a spike in tail latency on canary this morning, probably the same. did anyone bisect to commit?

kevin.w: I started a bisect, suspecting commit 8a3b2f1 from FA. local microbench: 7% p99 regression for seq=2048, bs=1 on A100.

linh.n: can you paste the repro? i'll try on nx.

kevin.w: sure — quick repro:
```bash
python -m bench.attn \  
  --model llama-2-7b \  
  --seq 2048 \  
  --batch 1 \  
  --kernel flash_attn_v2 
```

kevin.w: numbers (median of 10 runs): master w/our patch = 110ms, upstream 8a3b2f1 = 118ms. memory footprint unchanged.

maria.g: important detail — only happens on quantized int8 path with fused qkv layout, fp16 path seems fine. could be epilog reorder preventing some vectorized ops.

sam.k: okay could be xFormers recent API change too — they rewrote some fused-call wrappers last week. we track 3 upstreams here: FA, vLLM, xFormers. need plan to coordinate.

maria.g: proposal: (1) pin FA to 8a3b2f0 on hosted and dedicated canaries for next 48h, (2) open an upstream issue with perf profile + minimal reproducer, (3) add microbench CI gate for quantized path. any objections?

linh.n: +1 to gate. i'll add a perf CI job that runs lightweight kv-cache + seq 1024/2048 tests on PRs that touch kernels. should catch regressions quickly.

ci-bot: created perf-ci/job-quantized-quick (runs on linux-gpu-small). status: queued.

kevin.w: i'll draft the upstream issue and include flamegraphs & perf counter dumps. need to collect L2 miss samples — can someone run pwr profiling on canary? @ops-bot?

ops-bot: ping received. will schedule a 30min slot on canary-A100 in 30m and dump `nvprof` + `nsys` output to S3:/redwood/perf/1918765432/

sam.k: another angle — vLLM recently changed KV cache eviction when using paged attention; that interacts with our batching heuristics. noticed higher cache churn on multi-user workloads. has anyone correlated increased requests per second with the new eviction thresholds?

maria.g: not yet. I instrumented our runtime last night: observed +12% cache misses for sessions with many short-turn chats (avg seq 256) after the vLLM patch. likely eviction policy more aggressive.

linh.n: can you paste sample trace?

maria.g: sample trace (abbreviated):
```
[2026-03-17T09:02:12Z] session=usr_234 alloc kv_cache=512MB used=420MB evict_count=37
[2026-03-17T09:02:13Z] session=usr_235 alloc kv_cache=512MB used=490MB evict_count=62
[2026-03-17T09:02:14Z] session=usr_234 miss=true kvc_lookup_time=3.2ms
```

maria.g: those misses explain latency tail for small-turn workloads. suggestion: adjust eviction_threshold from 0.85 -> 0.92 for paged attention (temporary).

sam.k: sounds reasonable as short-term mitigation. but we should test mem pressure regressions. linchpin: ensure we don't OOM during bursts.

kevin.w: i'll run a stress job with 200 concurrent short sessions on dedicated to validate threshold tweak.

linh.n: on the FA side, i opened GH issue: https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attn/issues/4212 — included repro, flamegraph, and kernel traces. asked upstream to check their epilog reorder and vectorized store patterns.

maria.g: nice. add a note to test kernels built with nvcc 12 vs 13 — some codepaths change with compiler intrinsic availability.

kevin.w: noted. i'll build both variants in CI matrix for the microbench job.

sam.k: we also need a coordinated rollback plan if upstream pushes another change that regresses further. Ops: can we hotpatch our canary to fall back to fused-attn-vendor-kernel when p99 > threshold?

ops-bot: implemented feature toggle: `runtime.kernels.fallback_policy` — options: `none`, `model_compat`, `latency_guard`. applied `latency_guard` on canary. will flip off if false positives appear.

maria.g: great — set the guard to 1.15 x baseline at first. monitor for 24h.

kevin.w: quick note on perf CI outputs — please avoid huge artifacts. store condensed summaries + flamegraph pngs. S3 path layout: s3://redwood-ci/perf/1918765432/{job,summary,flame}.

linh.n: action items:
- kevin: finish bisect + post detailed perf counters (L2/L1/CUDA cycles) — due EOD
- sam: coordinate canary pin & rollback policy with ops — due 2h
- maria: open internal RFC for kv eviction threshold change and perf gate — due EOD
- linch: maintain upstream issue and follow-up with FA maintainers

kevin.w: starting bisect now. will post findings inline.

sam.k: thanks all. keep notes in the eng-runtime perf board. once we have reproducer minimized we should ask FA for a perf patch or opt-out flag. :thumbsup:

maria.g: one more thing — add a tiny test to our correctness suite to ensure fused qkv produces same logits within epsilon after fallback. avoids subtle correctness drift when we flip kernels.

kevin.w: good call. adding test now.

ci-bot: perf-ci/job-quantized-quick completed: 6/10 tests passed, 4 flaky/timeouts. details: s3://redwood-ci/perf/1918765432/quantized-quick-summary.json

linh.n: will triage flakies tomorrow morning. thanks everyone for rapid sync.

maria.g: closing loop — we'll keep canary pinned for 48h, escalate to vendor if upstream doesn't respond in 24h.

sam.k: copy that.
